problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ given that 

$$
B[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), right-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $B:$ 

$$
B={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore $B$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $B$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P:$
$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
